recipes.name: Spinach Pesto Chicken Breasts
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons basil pesto, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Mix spinach and pesto together in a bowl. Spread 1/2 of the mixture into the bottom of a glass baking dish and place chicken on top. Spread remaining spinach mixture over chicken. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.

Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Uncover and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over chicken. Return to the oven and bake until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Pesto Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This easy spinach pesto chicken recipe is made just 4 ingredients: boneless chicken breasts, fresh spinach, prepared basil pesto, and Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: This is a good base recipe. I followed other reviewers suggestions. I added the following: 4T of pesto (instead of 2), 1 t minced garlic & 1 t white wine to the pesto mix. I layered in with the chicken: 1/2 a chopped onion, 1/2 a roasted pepper (chopped), mushrooms. Amazing!!!! Don't forget to sprinkle the chicken breasts with some salt and pepper. Next time I'm thinking I'll add some grilled asparagus (anything to get more veggies in our diet!) Thanks for the excellent starting point!

My husband and I both enjoyed this. I wanted to make something quick and easy with food I had on hand -- spinach and chicken breasts. So I was happy to find this recipe. I'm sure it would have been excellent exactly as written but I had sliced mushrooms to use so I added them the last 15 minute when I added the cheese. For cheese I added some feta with the parmesan just because I was almost out of fresh parmesan. Followed cooking directions exactly and the chicken was yummy & moist and spinach with pesto delightful. When I make this again I will at least double the pesto and spinach because it cooks down so much, my husband and I were fighting over it. Probably plenty though for "normal" people. :)

This was good, but the chicken didn't have a lot of flavor unless you ate a piece with pesto on it. I even seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides before setting it on the spinach-pesto mix. The recipe called for 45 total minutes of cooking, which would have likely dried it out, so I just went by temperature, and it was done in the approximately 30 minutes of being covered with foil. I might try additional seasoning if I try it again.

The first time we made this, it was awful. The spinach is so over cooked it is unpalatable. The second time we made it was much better. Instead of baking, I pan cooked cubed chicken with garlic and butter, tossed in the pesto to just warm, then the spinach at the last minute - to just wilt the spinach. I used significantly more pesto than 2T - probably closer to 5 or 6. 

Served over fettuccine.

Dinner was on the table in 20 minutes.

Asparagus finely chopped, Cole slaw mix, garlic, wine,, Italian seasoning, more pesto. 
Veggies cooked way down. 
Added provolone cheese on top at the end, browned it little bit, yum.

This is an awesome recipe, a true 5 star restaurant quality & thank you so much for sharing it with us all. Based on other reviews, added, 1 cup of chopped red onions, 2 cups sliced baby Bella's, 1/2 cup of white wine & a tiny bottle of chopped pimento to pesto/spinach mix (which I doubled). Used 2 chicken breasts only as they were large. Sprinkled the breasts with salt, pepper & garlic powder. Served it with basmati rice.

Glad that I read the previous reviews and added more pesto, 3-4 minced garlic since my family likes it and white wine. I didn't have fresh spinach so I used frozen spinach thawed and squeezed the excess water and I made this with chicken thigh. Sprinkled some salt and pepper on the chicken before putting the spinach mix on top. Opted to make it with no cheese.

Delicious and So Easy! I did use a bit more pesto than called for and added garlic and white wine to the pesto sauce. I also seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper prior to spreading the pesto mixture on it. Served with pasta mixed with pesto and a green salad.

I followed other suggestions using salt and pepper on the chicken breasts. I marinated the chicken breasts in the pesto all day. I added some thin strips of zuchinni to the spinach as well as chopped onion and garlic. It turned out juicy, tender, and very flavorful.

I actually bought a gourmet pesto and smothered the chicken. I let it marinate in the refrigerator for an hour or so and then placed dry roasted tomatoes on top. I followed the cooking directions exactly and my meal came out perfect. Even having it left over at the same temperature in the oven was fine. Just cover it. My chicken breast were thick. I didn't need to add anything because the pesto had everything including the cheese and the pinenuts.

I added 2 cloves of chopped garlic to the pestos and spinach and coated the chicken in creole sauce, covered in foil and cooked on 170 for 45 mins. It was delicious! will definitely make again, maybe topping with chopped mushrooms next time.
I followed the recipe . Was dry and needed seasoning. I had way too much basil in my garden this year, will try again
I loved the recipie. It was so simple to make, easy to do, and was defiantly delicious.
I added salt, pepper and garlic to the chicken and topped it with chopped spinach, pesto and a can of drained artichoke hearts. Served over cauliflower rice.

I found it bland. Next time I will put salt, pepper & garlic powder in my breast. The flavors were great though. I added mushrooms & artichoke hearts. I tripled the pesto & added more chopped spinach.
Delicious starter recipe. I doubled the pesto! Now I know the base recipe I can add other ingredients. I put parm on half and grated Swiss on the other. Both worked for us.
Added, salt, pepper, to chicken breast minced garlic, onion in pesto sauce and doubled the spinach and pesto. Delicious
This was fine on its own, but I added mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, and artichoke hearts. It is easily one of our favorite dishes now, over rice or couscous!
I used paprika pesto instead of basil for more flavour and added a little white wine. I was amazing, definately adding it to my rotation for easy chicken dinners!
